9	UE procedure for reporting control information

If a UE transmits a PUSCH with repetitions over one or more slots or multiple PUSCHs over one or more slots that are scheduled by a DCI format, and the UE would transmit a PUCCH with HARQ-ACK and/or CSI information over a single slot that overlaps with the PUSCH transmission in the one or more slots, and the PUSCH transmission in the one or more slots fulfills the conditions in clause 9.2.5 for multiplexing the HARQ-ACK and/or CSI information, the UE multiplexes the HARQ-ACK and/or CSI information in the PUSCH transmission in the one or more slots. The UE does not multiplex HARQ-ACK and/or CSI information in the PUSCH transmission in a slot from the one or more slots if the UE would not transmit a single-slot PUCCH with HARQ-ACK and/or CSI information in the slot in case the PUSCH transmission was absent.
If a UE transmits a PUSCH with repetition Type B and the UE would transmit a PUCCH with HARQ-ACK and/or CSI information over a single slot that overlaps with the PUSCH transmission in one or more slots, the UE expects all actual repetitions of the PUSCH transmission [6, TS 38.214] that would overlap with the PUCCH transmission to fulfill the conditions in clause 9.2.5 for multiplexing the HARQ-ACK and/or CSI information, and the UE multiplexes the HARQ-ACK and/or CSI information in the earliest actual PUSCH repetition of the PUSCH transmission that would overlap with the PUCCH transmission and includes more than one symbol. The UE does not expect that all actual repetitions that would overlap with the PUCCH transmission do not include more than one symbol.
If the PUSCH transmission repetitions over the one or moreslots isare scheduled by a DCI format that includes a DAI field, or if the multiple PUSCH transmissions over the one or more slots are scheduled by a DCI format that includes a DAI field, the value of the DAI field is separately applicable for multiplexing HARQ-ACK information in any PUSCH repetition or transmission, respectively, in any slot from the one or more slots where the UE multiplexes HARQ-ACK information.

records.tr.scope: The study on physical layer use cases captured in [5] shows potentials for AI/ML algorithm in cellular communication system. Further study on using AI/ML for UE mobility in NR was hence conducted in this study item. This study explores RRM measurement and measurement event prediction mainly in temporal domain (FR1 for case B and FR2 for case A) and frequency domain (FR1) to understand the feasibility and performance of using AI/ML algorithm for enabling measurement reduction or handover performance improvement based on simulation evaluation. Analysis on specification impact is carried out for both UE sided model and network sided model for said scenarios.

Proposal 5: When deciding to stop the ongoing SDT procedure and to move UE into RRC connected mode, the gNB-CU-CP shall send Bearer Context Modification message, reusing existing codepoint (resume) in Bearer Context Status Change IE to resume all DRB.

Discussion:
Proposal 1: 	To confirm the understanding that:
-	For the DC architecture(s) that connects to NextGen Core (case 1 and 3), the Flow Based QoS framework is applied.
-	For the DC architecture that connects to EPC (case 2), LTE QoS framework (i.e., bearer based QoS) is applied.

Proposal 3:	In the DC architecture connecting to EPC, the NR gNB applies LTE QoS framework towards the EPC, LTE eNB and UE:
-	LTE DC procedures (e.g., SeNB addition, etc.) are applied when adding NR gNB as secondary eNB, in which necessary QoS service (i.e., bearer) are configured.
-	E-RAB (and concerning S1-U bearer) is established between EPC and NR gNB for SCG split bearer option according to LTE specification
-	X2-U is established between LTE eNB and NR gNB for split bearer option according to LTE specification
-	DRB is established between NR gNB and UE according to SCG bearer option or split bearer option as specified LTE

R3-162967	Extending XwAP for eLWIP
					Source: Ericsson LM
Discussion:
Proposal 1: All information required to be exchanged between the eNB and the LWIP-SeGW is UE-associated and is orthogonal to existing information currently exchanged for LWA.
Proposal 2: No non-UE-associated information seems to be strictly needed for LWIP; this would be true also in case a new interface was to be specified for LWIP.
Proposal 3: The current WT-Initiated WT Modification procedure can be used to e.g. request a change of UP TNL address from the WT.
Proposal 4: In case the WT supports LWA only, LWIP only, or both and, the current Xw Setup can be reused without changes.
Proposal 5: RAN3 should discuss the options for Xw Setup and agree on the most suitable way forward.
Proposal 6: In case no BSSIDs were signaled at Xw Setup, WT resource status reporting cannot be used; however, this is an issue also with current LWA.
Proposal 7: Reuse the current WT Release procedures for LWIP.
Proposal 8: In case the WT supports LWA but not LWIP, it shall fail LWIP Addition Preparation; in case the WT supports LWIP but not LWA, it shall fail WT Addition Preparation.
Proposal 9: If the WT supports both LWA and LWIP and it receives an LWIP ADDITION REQUEST message concerning a UE for which LWA is ongoing, it shall fail that procedure, and vice versa.
Proposal 10: Discuss and agree the CRs in [5] and [6].
Intel: Xw setup can be reused is contradicting other parts of the proposal
Intel: currently each AP supports LWIP REL-13, this will not be the case in REL-14

Broadcom: there is no REL-14 LWIP requirements

records.reason: To enable delta configuration during DU change without mandating CU to read CellGroupConfig IE from DU.
MaxnoofBPLMNs is not aligned with TS 38.331
PDCCH Blind Detection should be coordinated between the MCG and the SCG.

For CA based PDCP duplication, gNB-DU shall setup two RLC entities if gNB-CU provides two UL UP TNL Information IEs. When gNB-CU decides to disable CA based PDCP duplication, it needs to inform gNB-DU in order for it to remove the  RLC entity associated with the secondary path. For DC based PDCP duplication, gNB-CU shall also inform gNB-DU about disabling of it, in order for gNB-DU to stop activate/deactivate PDCP duplication by MAC CE. Besides,  the existing message could not support reconfiguring the existing DRBs to either CA based or DC based PDCP duplication.

Since the resource coordination over X2 interface for the purpose of LTE-NR spectrum sharing has been agreed in RAN3#99bis meeting, some related information transferring to gNB-DU should be standardized as well.

It was agreed that during the bearer context management procedures, the CU-CP may provide the wrong DRB ID (e.g., Multiple DRB ID Instances or Unknown DRB ID) to the CU-UP, in which case the CU-UP set up such DRB(s) or modify such DRB(s) unsuccessfully. Thus,  the cause value “Multiple DRB ID Instances” and “Unknown DRB ID” is introduced to the E1 interface to enable the CU-CP to know the reason for the unsuccessful estabilishment/modification. During the UE context management procedures, the CU may also provide the wrong DRB ID to the DU, which will result in unsuccessful estabilishment/modification. However, there is no cause calue to indicate this abnomal case.

In TS 38.323, either 12 or 18bits are supported for NR PDCP SN. For EN-DC case, PDCP-config is contained in mcg-RB-Config of CG-ConfigInfo. It is agreed that, gNB-CU will provide CG-ConfigInfo in CU to DU RRC information for EN-DC case. However, it depends on implementation whether gNB-CU will forward all the information of CG-ConfigInfo to gNB-DU. e.g., gNB-CU may only forward lower layer related information of CG-ConfigInfo to gNB-DU. For standalone case, there’s no way for gNB-CU to provide PDCP-Config to gNB-DU as it is assumed that gNB-DU can’t fetch RRC reconfiguration message for the UE. While in 38.425, gNB-DU needs to know PDCP SN in order to feedback the highest transmitted/delivered PDCP SN.

RLC mode could be changed and reconfigured by DRB release/addition (including RLC bearer release) or full configuration. At RAN3 #101bis meeting, this RLC mode change issue was discussed offline, and some conclusions were made, including that RLC mode should be added in DRB To Be Modified List in the UE Context Modification Request message on F1 interface.
Protected-EUTRA-Resources-ItemIEs is defined as a single continer, but the content is multiple IEs.

RAN2 agreed that the UE whose current active BWP is not configured with a CSS should receive the updated system information by dedicated RRC signalling. In the current version of CU/DU split scenario, the CU does not know whether the current active BWP is configured with a CSS or not. Therefore does not know whether it should generate dedicated RRC messages.
When RLC failure occurs for the CA duplication, the CU doesn’t know the Scell(s) associated to the RLC entity with failure.
To add text and IEs for the removal of SCTP association over F1

1/ In the LS S2-187355 SA2 has indicated to RAN3 that SA2 foresees some scenarios where a dynamically assigned 5QI can be associated when signalling non-standardized or non-preconfigured QoS profiles.  

2/ 5QI information elements are not extensible, unlike other elements of the 5QI descriptor.
The presence for DRB information (the NG-RAN part of QoS information) is mandatory in tabular but optional in ASN.1. This information should be mandatory.

Per TS38.104, TDD Band can be configured with asymmetric UL and DL,i.e, n50 for TDD. However, the existing Served Cell Information IE the UL and DL bandwidth for TDD can only be set to symmetric. Therefore, it is need to introduce a new UL and DL Transmission Bandwidth for asymmetric TDD Band.
RAN2 agreed to extend the RANAC size to 8bits for future proof.

1. The MgNB-DU should be possible to provide its own PHR MAC CE format toward the MgNB-CU, when working in DC mode.
2. The presence conditions of the field “DRX Long Cycle Start Offset” and “DRX Config” in the “DU to CU RRC Information” IE are unclear, which may confuse the reader.
The (M)gNB-DU should transfer the DRX offset to the (M)gNB-CU, or otherwise it cannot include it into the CGConfigInfo IE to be delivered to the S-NG-RAN node.

An unique identifier needs to be transferred between the NG-RAN nodes in order to do correlation of logs for a given UE in case of disaggregated gNB deployment. This identifier can be combined with other IDs present on both E1 and F1

In current TS38.473, the Write-Replace Warning procedure can transmit one SIB message only at a time. If segmentation is applied to a warning message, multiple Write-Replace Warning procedures should be triggered to transmit one warning message. This procedure is inefficient for warning message considering its urgency.

In the MeasConfig configured to the UE, MeasGapSharingConfig is used to define the scheme for sharing gaps when UE is required to perform different types of gap-needed measurements, which was introduced by RAN2 for R15.
In CU-DU architecture, gaps are generated by DU and sent to CU. However, in the current DU to CU RRC Information, MeasGapConfig is included whereas MeasGapSharingConfig is missing.

On the other hand, in SIB1, SI-SchedulingInfo contains the systemInformationAreaID, which are used by UE to check whether it needs to re-acquire the area-specific SI or not. Besides, the areaScope is associated with each other SI to indicate whether the other SI is cell-specific or area-specific. In current specification, gNB-CU sends SIB type, SIB message and value tag of other SI to gNB-DU, and gNB-DU encodes SI-SchedulingInfo of other SI in SIB1.

The current ASN.1 for Latest RRC version IE erroneously use bit string instead of octet string. This makes it impossible to use the existing IE for the intended functionality

The DRB Activity IE in UE INACTIVITY NOTIFICATION is mandatory in tabular but optional in ASN.1
An NR Cell may be confgured with different SCSs for the SS Block than indicated in the NR Transmission Bandwidth information.
This is the rapporteur updates for non-controversial issues found in the latest version of the specification

Cell Type IE is mandatory present in the UE history information IE, which is also mandatory IE, during Xn/NG handover procedure. In CU-DU split case, gNB-CU sets the Cell type. However, the cell type is normally configured to the gNB-DU since serving cell informaiton is configured to gNB-DU.
3-byte TAC (5GS TAC) is not required for EN-DC. RAN2#102 therefore agreed to optionally include TAC (3-byte) in NR SIB1. Need to update network interfaces accordingly.

For Choice, the current ASN.1 
uses ProtocolExtensionContainer where a ProtocolIE-SingleContainer is more suitable since only one IE shall be included.
uses ellipsis (...) where this is not needed since the extension container is in place
Currently the gNB-CU system information was speicified as a container, which could not fullfill the operation that a specific SIB could be updated/stopped.
Addition of functionality over the F1 to enable the CU to indicate to the DU that the rate of incoming UEs need to be reduced.

There is some misalignments between the tabular and the ASN.1. This is the rapporteur CR to correct remaining misalignments.

Paging: Some IEs are marked as optional in ASN.1 but they are required for paging
DRB-Notify-List: Should be a range SIZE(1.. maxnoofDRBs)

In MR-DC scenario both the MN and the SN may be split into CU and DUs. For the SN side, when the MN or SN-CU wishes to provide some information toward the SN-DU, e.g. the CellGroupConfig of the SCG at source side during SN change or intra-SgNB-CU SgNB-DU change, such information shall be delivered to the SN-DU via the RRC container CGConfigInfo.
For the MN side (i.e. how to provide some information toward the MgNB-DU), however, the case is not clear. In early specifications designed for Stand Alone scenario such information seems delivered directly as separate F1AP IEs, but now in MR-DC scenario these F1AP IEs cannot fully meet the demand, especially for low layer coordination between the MCG and the SCG.

UE-associated LTE/NR resource coordination requires information specific to the E-UTRA cell in the gNB-DU. The MeNB Cell ID (PCell) must be available in the gNB-DU at UE context setup. Need to improve error handling.

PWS system information are broadcast in SIB 6/7/8 as specified in 38.331, i.e. SIB6 contains an ETWS primary notification, SIB7 for ETWS secondary notification and SIB for CMAS notification, they are coded in gNB-CU, while gNB-DU is in charge of scheduling these SIB blocks in SI. 
Current spec the gNB-CU sends SI to gNB-DU, which actually is not precise since gNB-CU doesn’t know in which SI gNB-DU will finally put and schedule these SIB blocks.
In NGAP message, the Cell List for Restart is M in PWS RESTART INDICATION message, while O in F1AP message, which is inconsistent with each other.

When the AMF releases the UE using the UE Context Release Command because of an error in the NAS layer or in the AMF this cannot be indicated to DU in the UE Context Release Command over the F1 interface. An example is when the AMF as indicates ‘Authentication failure’. To simplify trouble shooting it is helpful if the information related to a failure could indicate that the problem is not related to an error in RAN.

There is also an editorial error for the ‘Unspecified’ cause in the ´Miscellaneous cause’ category which is described as “Sent when none of the above cause values applies and the cause is not related to any of the categories Radio Network Layer, Transport Network Layer, NAS or Protocol.”. There is no NAS category over F1 hence referring to the NAS category is not correct.
Paging origin IE is missing in the F1 specification

It has been introduced in the Transmission Stop Indicator IE the “stop” and also “restart” additionally. However the description of the IE still has only the “This IE indicates the gNB-DU to stop the data transmission for the UE.”
Further, since the “restart” was introduced in addition to “stop”, the name of this IE (Transmission Stop Indicator IE) is misleading.

(for ref, this “restart” was introduced by R3-184367)

1. P-max coordination on FR2 is not supported in F1AP.
2. gNB-DU initiated band combination / feature set negotiation is not supported in F1AP.
3. “drx-SlotOffset” coordination is not supported in F1AP.

In RAN2#103bis meeting, on measurement gap configuration, the following agreements are reached:
Measurement gap coordination for NE-DC:
MN->SN: per UE or FR1 gap pattern
SN->MN: gap request (without frequency list),a need for gap IE is introduced in CG-CONFIG
Measurement gap coordination for NR-DC:
MN->SN: the configured per-UE or FR1 or FR2 measurement gap pattern and the gap purpose
SN -> MN: a list of SN configured frequencies in FR1 and FR2 measured by the UE
Following above agreements,in the email discuss in RAN2,i.e. [104#33][NR/Late drop] INMs,the measurement gap related parameters have been introduced in the inter-node message.
Based on RAN2 agreements and definition on inter-node message,the related F1 spec also needs some udpate.

RAN2 confirms that for SRB duplication the network may configure duplication in the DL only, in which case all UL transmission should be made through the logical channel of the primary path, so gNB-CU needs to fill the LCID of primary path into PDCP-Config IE. gNB-DU allocates LCIDs for SRB, and the consensus is not to mandate gNB-CU to read CellGroupConfig which contains LCID. It is suggested gNB-DU determines the LCID for the primary path and provides LCID over F1 interface.

gNB-DU encodes CellGroupConfig, which may contain the servingCellMO (i.e., MeasObjectId) of each serving cell. There’s no way for gNB-DU to acquire the mapping relationship between MeasObjectId and serving cell from MeasConfig provided by gNB-CU.

In RAN2#101meeting,PH-TypeListSCG IE is introduced in CG-Config which is used to indicate the type of Power Headroom in SCG cells.Since it is physical layer related parameter,it should be generated by gNB-DU and send to gNB-CU.

There were some issues detected during the implementation phase of changes related to CLI: 
IntendedTDD-DL-ULConfig: missing Slot-Configuration-List
SymbolAllocInSlot: name numDLULsymbols not aligned with tabular
TDD-Info: IntendedTDD-DL-ULConfig: added in NBC way
A sentence in descriptive IE text contains text describing sending side behaviour and could be removed(aligned with similar proposed change in Xn)

The HandoverPreparationInformation can include the sidelink related UE information in the scenarios below. 
For the inter-gNB-CU handover, the gNB-CU receives a HandoverPreparationInformation from the source node so it seems the gNB-CU does not need to use an additional CG-ConfigInfo for the sidelink related UE information.
For the intra-gNB-CU inter-gNB-DU handover, if the sidelink UE related information is received from the source gNB-DU, the gNB-CU can also generate a HandoverPreparationInformation to include it for the target gNB-DU.    
The reference of UEAssistanceInformationEUTRA is not defined in TS38.331 and should be referred to TS36.331 instead of TS38.331.

The current values of the Measurement periodicity for UL and UL&DL positioning are as follows:

The measurement periodicity share the same IE with E-CID positioning measurement periodicity, which is aligned with UE RRM measurment report interval in RRC, which is as follows:

ReportInterval ::=                  ENUMERATED {ms120, ms240, ms480, ms640, ms1024, ms2048, ms5120, ms10240, ms20480, ms40960,
                                                    min1,min6, min12, min30 }

This is incorrect because that for UL and UL&DL positioning it is gNB to measure the SRS sent from the UE, while the RRM measurement is for the UE to measure DL reference signals. 

The SRS periodicity has the following values:


It is obvious that in the measurement periodicity, at least the following values are not aligned with the SRS periodicity: 120ms, 240ms, 480ms, 1024ms, 2048ms, 1min, 6min, 12min, and 30min.


Thus, the measurement periodicity for the UL and UL&DL positioning should be aligned with SRS periodicity, rather than the RRC report interval.
The values of SRS periodicity should be added in the measurement periodicity for UL and UL&DL positioning, including 160ms, 320ms, 1280ms 2560ms, 81920ms.

Some of the values in current measurement periodicity should be subtituded by the similar value that can be aligned with the SRS periodicity. For example, the value 1min should be subtituded by a similar value, such as 61440ms. The value of 6min, 12min, and 30min can be subtituted by a similar value such as 368640ms, 737280ms, and 1843200ms.

If SRS periodicity interval is not accurate, there will be some redudency in mesurements, inacurate reporting, shifting of the report measurements update, that could not be deteced by the LMF. As conscequence the report could be totally incurate …

For E-UTRA Cells, we include one “EARFCN” (indicating the central frequency of the transmission band) and one “transmission bandwidth” per UL/DL/TDD within the “Cell Information” IEs. These two IEs are enough to deduce the exact location of the entire transmission band, i.e. the frequency of the lowest carrier and the highest carrier.
For NR Cells we include one “NR ARFCN” (indicating the “Point A” rather than the central frequency), one SCS and one “transmission bandwidth” per UL/DL/TDD within the “Cell Information” IEs.
However, the mechanism to determine the frequency raster has changed a lot for NR cells compared with E-UTRA ones, making these parameters far not enough to deduce the location of the entire transmission band, e.g. lack of the “offset to carrier” to indicate the frequency of the lowest carrier.
For the UL,it has been corrected in Rel-16 SON/MDT WI.However,for DL,it is suggested to correct via a separate CR.

In EN-DC case, to support CP-UP separation, the F1-C transfer path can be configured to the IAB node. In TS38.331, such configuration is included in CellGroupConfig IE, which is generated by the DU of parent node. In this sense, the current specification assumes that the F1-C transfer path is determined by the DU of the parent node. However, our original intention is to let IAB donor CU make the decision. Thus, the current spec. is not aligned with our original intention. Moreover, the parent node is not a suitable entity to determine F1-C transfer path since it does not have the full-picture of LTE leg and NR leg. 

With above considerations, some revisions to the current specification are needed for F1-C transfer path configuration.

In the current NR-PRS Beam Information IE, the PRS Resource Set ID is included, but there is no resource ID:


The NR-PRS Beam Informatrion provides the beam angle information for each PRS resource. The UE can measure the PRS and report the measurement results for each PRS resource to the LMF for the DL-AoD positioning. For example, the UE can report the following information in the LPP message Provide Location Information.
NR-DL-AoD-MeasElement-r16 ::= SEQUENCE {
	dl-PRS-ID-r16					INTEGER (0..255),
	nr-PhysCellID-r16				NR-PhysCellID-r16						OPTIONAL,
	nr-CellGlobalID-r16				NCGI-r15								OPTIONAL,
	nr-ARFCN-r16					ARFCN-ValueNR-r15						OPTIONAL,
	nr-DL-PRS-ResourceID-r16		NR-DL-PRS-ResourceID-r16	 			OPTIONAL,
	nr-DL-PRS-ResourceSetID-r16		NR-DL-PRS-ResourceSetID-r16 			OPTIONAL,
	nr-TimeStamp-r16				NR-TimeStamp-r16,
	nr-DL-PRS-RSRP-Result-r16		INTEGER (0..126),
	nr-DL-PRS-RxBeamIndex-r16		INTEGER (1..8)							OPTIONAL,
	nr-DL-AoD-AdditionalMeasurements-r16
									NR-DL-AoD-AdditionalMeasurements-r16	OPTIONAL,
	...
}

Then LMF can then match the measurements to the PRS angle information based on the NR-PRS Beam Information IE of the TRP. The LMF can then calculate the AoD information and further calculate the UE location.

In order the enable the LMF to match the measurements per PRS resource to the PRS angle, the “PRS Angle Item” should include the PRS resource ID information. Otherwise, an easier way can have the clarification in the semantics description, such as, “The PRS angle items are associated with the PRS resource in the ascending order in each resource set”. 

Thus, two options can be considered:
Option 1: Add the “Resource ID” IE in each “PRS Angle Item” IE.
Option 2: Add the semantics description for the “PRS Angle Item” IE: “The PRS angle items are associated with the PRS resource in the ascending order in each resource set”.
This CR provides the solution of Option 2.

Rev1: group as preference for option 1, Option 1 is implemented

In TS38.401, a NOTE is given for inter-gNB-DU mobility as below:
This note indicates that the source gNB-DU will perform as normal case (non-handover) for data packet transmission, i.e., 
gNB-CU continuously sends DL packets of DAPS bearers to the source gNB-DU
Source gNB-DU continuously schedules DL resource for packet transmission of DAPS and non-DAPS bearers, where packets include the ones already buffered at the source gNB-DU for both DAPS and non-DAPS bearers and the ones from gNB-CU for DAPS bearers
Source gNB-DU continuously schedules UL resource for packet transmission of DAPS and non-DAPS bearers
These behaviors are not aligned with the intention of DAPS handover, and may cause that: non-DAPS bearers may interrupt the data transmission of DAPS bearers

To solve the above problem, it is better to allow the source gNB-DU know the data transmission of which bearers should be stopped during the DAPS handover procedure.

In Rel-17, RAN2 have introduced Non-Cell-Defining SSB (NCD-SSB) dedicated for RedCap UE. One Bandwidth Part (BWP) can have up to one SSB (CD-SSB or NCD-SSB). BWP with NCD-SSB is in different frequency from CD-SSB. Hence, servingCellMOs pointing to NCD-SSB or CD-SSB are different.
However, in F1AP there is only one servingCellMO IE assigned by CU and signalled in the UE CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST and UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST message to inform DU of UE’s servingCellMO to use for legacy CD-SSB. This means, when CU delivers servingCellMO to DU in the F1 request message, CU doesn’t know if DU will choose active BWP with NCD-SSB or CD-SSB for UE. It is proposed to update F1AP by adding an optional list of candidate servingCellMOs, i.e., servingCellMO List IE to be used for NCD-SSBs, with both servingCellMO and SSB frequency info so that after DU chooses the active BWP for the UE, the DU can select related measObjectId as servingCellMO for NCD-SSB using the new list IE instead of impacting legacy servingCellMO IE that is used for CD-SSB.

Furthermore, feedback from DU to CU over F1AP is needed so that CU knows which MeasObjectIDs will be used by DU and CU can free up the resources for those unused measObjectIds for a given UE. CU will also be able to determine the need of Measurement Gaps based on DU selected BWPs.
.

CT1 and SA2 has specifed a feature referred to as MINT (Minimization of Service Interruption). This feature allows UEs of a PLMN which is experiencing so called "disaster conditions" to roam in other networks. Such type of roaming is called disaster roaming.

In TS 38.331, RAN2 agrees to introduce SIB15 containing Provision of disaster roaming information, which enables network to indicate which PLMNs' UEs are allowed to do disaster roaming.

The information contained in SIB15 may be useful at the gNB-CU to enable awarenes of the gNB-DUs and the PLMNs supporting disaster roaming. This may allow the gNB-CU to set the UAC asistance information appropriately.

This CR provides the functional support of the MINT.

pre-configured MGs are applicable to both RedCap and non-RedCap UEs

Considering the Rel-17 restriction of one pre-MG, to support the preconfigured gap for all the configured BWPs, the following actions are needed:
The gNB-DU should inform gNB-CU of the list of all configured BWPs information 
Based on the BWP information received from gNB-DU, the gNB-CU requests gNB-DU to generate the pre-configured measurement GAP for all the configured BWPs in CGC. To avoid generating any RRC Reconfiguration message at this step, the gNB-CU should ignore the received CGC from the gNB-DU. 
The gNB-DU schedules the preconfigured Measurement GAP and signals the information to gNB-CU together with the contents of the new generated CGC. Based on this, the gNB-CU sends the preconfigured MG and CGC to UE via RRC signaling

Timing Error Group (TEG) was introduced in NRPPa/F1AP at RAN3#115 based on RAN1 agreements, and some corrections agreed at RAN3#116 (CR0063r4) to further align with RAN1/RAN2 decisions.

At RAN3#117e, an LS was received from RAN4 (R3-224216) listing agreements on timing error margins for UE/TRP Tx/Rx/RxTx TEGs. Based on the RAN4 agreements, RAN3 added timing error margin associated to the UE/TRP Tx/Rx/RxTx TEGs. Because the timing error margins were introduced as a late correction to complete the TEG framework, the IEs were made optional in order to be backwards compatible but an FFS captured on how to interpret the absence of margin values.

In fact, the sender (UE/gNB) must always know the timing error margins if it is supporting TEG as a feature, and there is no scenario where it makes sense for the TRP/gNB to omit the margin. The only reason the IEs are optional is that they were introduced as a backwards compatible correction to the incomplete TEG framework, which was unfortunately introduced piecemeal in NRPPa/F1AP due to agreements being reached in RAN1 and RAN4 at different meetings.

For the TEG framework to work without undue complexity, the timing error margins should be mandatory to avoid abnormal conditions.

Following the RAN1 agreement, SRS resource IDs have been introduced for aggregated measurement. However, solely relying on the SRS resource ID is insufficient for identifying the carrier to which the SRS resources are linked.

In Rel-18 LTM, the TCI states configuration are only included when early synchronization is requested, but they are also required during a cell switch (since the LTM cell switch MAC CE includes a TCI state which the UE should use). If no TCI state list is configured for an LTM candidate, an LTM cell switch MAC CE indicating that TCI state cannot be executed by the UE since the UE would not have any TCI state to refer to and the result would be that the procedure will fail. To ensure TCI state information is always available for cell switch, it should be included beyond early synchronization. Therefore, we propose adding a new IE in the F1AP LTM Configuration Information IE to reference it.

The LTM can coexist with the feature of MIMO with 2TA. In particular, one cell can have two TA values, each of which is associated with one TAG. In current F1AP signaling, the TAG information of TA value of the candidate cell is provided from the candidate gNB-DU to the source gNB-DU via gNB-CU in the DU-CU TA INFORMATION TRANSFER and CU-DU TA INFORMATION TRANSFER messages. 
To avoid triggering PDCCH order to obtain TA of candidate cell(s) in target gNB-DU, source gNB-DU can transfer valid TA information to target gNB-DU when LTM is triggered. Therefore, the valid TA value can be reused in target gNB-DU for the following LTM execution. However, the TAG information of TA value is not provided.
To support NCR in disaggregated architecture, it is needed for the gNB-CU to provide NCR authorized information to the gNB-DU.

Rel-18 Intra-CU LTM specified two mechanisms of pre-calculating UL TA values for faster RACH-less access to a candidate cell (called “early TA acquisition”): 
NW obtains UL TA values of candidate cells before cell switch (by PDDCH-ordering the UE to initiate RACH) and configures the pre-acquired TA value to the UE in the LTM Cell Switch Command. 
 “UE-based TA measurements”, where CU configures the UE to derive UL TA on its own based on the Rx timing difference between the current serving cell and candidate cell, together with the current TA value. 

The second mechanism has been designed in a way that it cannot be used unless the serving DU explicitly indicates so (set to “FFF”) via LTM Cell Switch Command (even though configured to the UE via RRC by CU). However, DU is currently obvilous of whether CU configured the UE-based TA measurements to the UE and for which cells. As a result, the serving DU (who is not aware) won’t be able to indicate the UE to use it at all. Instead, it will execute the first mechanism for a candidate cell (for which the UE-based TA measurement has already been configured) to provide the TA value in the LTM Cell Switch Command, where the UE has to unnecessarily follow the PDCCH order and initiate RACH to that candidate cell. Due to its cascaded design, the UE-based TA measurement feature may not work as intended, if such configuration from CU is not known to DU who controls early RACH and decides cell switch.

The Candidate Cells To Be Cancelled List in the UE CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST is included as a conditional IE, but where the conditional text is expressed with a “may”. Further, the procedure text describes that if this IE is included: “only the resources reserved for the cells identified by the included NR CGIs are about to be released”
Conditional IEs are however mandatory if the condition is met so using a may statement and describing behaviour if absent does not comply with the principles of the specification. The error handling is specified in TS 38.413 section 10.3.3 as follows “If an IE/IE group is not included in a received message and the presence of the IE/IE group is mandatory or the presence is conditional and the condition is true according to the version of the specification used by the receiver, an abstract syntax error occurs due to a missing IE/IE group.”
In existing specification, it is currently not possible to use the intended functionality – to delete all if the IE is absent.

RAN3-123 meeting discussed the non-integer DRX cycle issue for XR in F1AP design and agreed that “For CU -> DU direction, no need to add a new IE”. And it is marked as “to be continued” about whether need behaviour text for gNB-DU is needed for non-integer DRX configuration. However, after some further checking, such agreement should be reverted due to the following reasons
In previous discussion for CU-DU split, it was agreed that CU decide DRX cycle length and the timer for short DRX cycle, while DU generate remaining parameters for DRX configuration. CU informs DU to setup DRX configuration by providing DRX parameters. The corresponding agreements from previous RAN3 meetings are pasted as following:
RAN3-97bis:
DRX Cycle length is controlled by CU
WA: All other DRX parameters are controlled by DU except timers which are FFS
RAN3-98:
CU->DU
RRC containers: SCG config info (name FFS pending RAN2), UE capabilities
List of target cells (PScell, SCG cell(s)) / NCGI of each cell which is going to serve the UE
Bearer list
DRX cycle length
In the semantics description, the sub IEs (i.e., Long DRX Cycle Length, Short DRX Cycle Length, Short DRX Cycle Timer) included in the DRX cycle IE are corresponded to the field preferredDRX-LongCycle, preferredDRX-ShortCycle and preferredDRX-ShortCycle Timer defined in RRC, separately. The correspondance means the format and value of these sub IEs are same as these fields defined in RRC specification, but not meaning that the CU send these UE preferred fields received from UAI to the gNB-DU and let the DU to decide which value to be used for the DRX cycle length and the timer for short DRX configuration. 
Therefore, to align with the principle that CU control the DRX Cycle length, R3 should introduce a new IE for non-integer DRX cycle in UE Context Management related procedures. In addition, to avoid cause further mis-understanding (e.g. CU provides UE preferred value on the DRX cycle while DU make the final decision), it is suggested to update the semantics description of the existing DRX Cycle IE and link it to the RRC field name contained in the DRX-Config IE.

In Rel-18, Validity Area Specific SRS Information IE was introduced in the Requested SRS Transmission Characteristics IE. The NG-RAN may take this information into account for configuring SRS transmissions for the UE in the indicated validity area during Positioning Information Exchange procedure, and/or may reserve the indicated SRS information during SRS Information Reservation Notification procedure. 
However, the current information contained in the Validity Area Specific SRS Information IE corresponds to only one SRS resource, which leads to the following situations,
During Positioning Information Exchange procedure, the LMF can recommend only one SRS resource for NG-RAN to configure SRS configuration containing multiple SRS resource sets and multiple SRS resources in each SRS resource set. Resulting in more chances for different NG-RAN node to allocate the same area-specific SRS resources for different UEs, which should be avoided.
During SRS Information Reservation Notification procedure, the LMF can notify the NG-RAN to reserve only one SRS resource in each SRS INFORMATION RESERVATION NOTIFICATION message, which is inefficient if the LMF needs to notify NG-RAN to reserve multiple SRS resources.

The LTM can coexist with the feature of MIMO with 2TA. In particular, one cell can have two TA values, each of which is associated with one TAG. In current F1AP signaling, the TA value of the candidate cell is provided from the candidate gNB-DU to the source gNB-DU via gNB-CU. However, the TAG information of TA value is not provided. As a result, the source gNB-DU cannot determine TAG ID of the received TA value, so that it cannot include the correct TA in the LTM cell switch command MAC CE.

In order to indicate temporary capabilities restriction, it was specified in TS 38.331 that: 
the gNB will configure musim-CandidateBandList-r18 to the UE for reporting temporary capabilities restriction, as the band-filter list.
in the UAI, the UE signals its temporary capabilities restrictions as forbidden band combinations with band indexed to the band-filter list and/or affected band combinations with band indexed to the band-filter list along with explicit fields for restricted (lower) capabilities e.g. maximum MIMO layers. 
Thus, the forbidden/affected band combinations need to combine the UAI and band-filter list provided by gNB.

In the CU/DU split architecture, the band-filter list is generated by the CU. When the CU receives MUSIM UAI from the UE, it should deliver it to the DU with the band-filter list together so that the DU can understand what the temporary capabilities restriction is to generate the proper configuration (e.g. MIMO layers configuration) based on UE temporary capabilities restriction. Otherwise, the DU cannot derive the forbidden/affected bands.

According to RAN1 parameter list and LPP TS 37.355, the linkage information ("Aggregated PRS Resource Set List") in the tabular for IE "PRS Configuration" should be per positioning frequency layer (PFL) (and not across Sets within a single PFL) and should therefore be moved up to the "PRS Resource Set List" level. 
To indicate the linkage information, in the "Aggregated PRS Resource Set List", the Point A and the DL-PRS Resource Set ID are currently used. However, there are the following issues:
The {Point A, Resource Set ID} alone does not define a PFL.
A single TRP can have up to 4 PFLs where each PFL can have up to 2 DL-PRS Resource Sets. DL-PRS Aggregation can be across 2 PFLs or 3 PFLs, as well as 2+2 PFLs (see e.g., RAN1 LS in R3-237136 (RAN3#122) and RAN1 parameter list). The latter (2+2 PFLs) can not be supported with the current structure.

1. SRS for Positioning with Tx Frequency Hopping for RedCap UEs, RAN1 agreed that the number of hops: ENUMERATED {2,3,4,5,6} (new IE).
However, in the F1AP, the value range of Number of Hops is defined as INTEGER(1..6), which should be corrected. NBC way was acceptable.

2. For Positioning SRS BW Aggregation, RAN1/RAN2 agreed that the number of “aggregated combinations” is up to 32, and for each combination, only one SRS resource set from each of the 2 or 3 carriers are aggregated, e.g. CC#1 SRS resource set 1 + CC#2 SRS resource set 2 + CC#3 SRS resource set 3. In F1AP, the Aggregated Positioning SRS Resource Set List IE includes at most 48 SRS resource sets to be aggregated in one combination, which equal to 3CCs * 16 SRS Resource sets per CC. It’s not well aligned with the design of TS 38.331, which may cause erroneous during SRS configuration.

This procedure was introduced for the scenario of multiple cell ID broadcast network sharing scenario, as the F1-U tunnel is not established with some gNB-CUs during Broadcast Context Setup procedure.

In previous RAN3 meeting, the UP-failure scenario was discussed, in such case, the gNB-DU may need to trigger the F1AP: Broadcast Transport Resource Request procedure towards the gNB-CU with which the shared F1-U tunnel has already been established. But in such case the gNB-CU handling is unclear, e.g., whether regard this as abnormal scenario, or release the already established F1-U tunnel and setup new one.

In this procedure, gNB-CU either instructs the gNB-DU to send a MAC CE command to the UE for cell switch, and/or trigger early DL or UL synchronization or to provide assistance information to the gNB-DU for triggering LTM procedures.

The Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics may include a "PRS Bandwidth Aggregation Request Indication" flag whose meaning is nowhere defined.

DL-PRS aggregation is defined across DL-PRS Resource Sets of different positioning frequency layers (PFLs), and a TRP may configure DL-PRS aggregation across 2, 3 or 2+2 PFLs.
A UE may indicate to the LMF the desired DL-PRS in the LPP IE NR-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Request. The LPP IE NR-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Request may include the IE NR-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Information, which defines the desired DL-PRS parameter (the UE can request these explicit DL-PRS parameter which are within the scope of previously provided (predefined) on-demand DL-PRS configurations (NR-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Configurations)). These DL-PRS parameter in LPP are the same as in the NRPPa/F1AP Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics. For DL-PRS aggregation, a UE may indicate in addition which NR-On-Demand-DL-PRS-Information elements are desired for aggregation. However, the corresponding functionality is missing in the Requested DL PRS Transmission Characteristics IE. Therefore, it is unclear how an gNB-CU can indicate to the gNB-DU which DL-PRS configuration information is requested/applicable for aggregation.
The TRP INFORMATION REQUEST message may include a request for available/supported on-demand DL-PRS information ('on-demand prs'). However, the corresponding response element On-demand PRS TRP Information (9.3.1.240) does not include any information on whether the on-demand PRS Request is allowed also for aggregated DL-PRS.
The TRP INFORMATION REQUEST message may include a "PRS Bandwidth Aggregation Request Indication" flag whose meaning is nowhere defined.

Peer UE ID is needed when CU request DU to provide configuration for a PC5 Relay RLC channel to be setup for L2 U2U relay operation, considering the following reasons:
When receiving a request from CU to configure PC5 Relay RLC channels for a L2 U2U Remote/Relay UE, DU should know which PC5 Relay RLC channels are belonging to the same peer UE so that to configure the logical channel configuration (e.g. priority, LCG ID) for each PC5 Relay RLC channel, e.g. to decide which PC5 Relay RLC channels/logical channels are configured to the same/different LCG. 
On the other hand, when receiving SL BSR from U2U UE, DU should identify the involved PC5 Relay RLC channels belonging to the LCG ID for the reported buffer size for a DST index and the LCH priority/configuration of each PC5 Relay RLC channel, to perform mode 1 resource allocation.  
  So, DU should know the association of the peer UE and the PC5 Relay RLC channel to make proper SL logical channel configuration and interpret the SL BSR correctly.

At RAN3#120 the scenario of large data volume during MO-SDT transaction presented in tdoc R3-232721 was acknowledged and also the need to investigate and select a solution to help gNB-CU CP determining when sending the UE to RRC_connected in this scenario.

In this CR the gNB-DU can inform the gNB-CU CP if large data size is detected (e.g. through BSR). The threshold for gNB-DU to consider the uplink data to be large and inform gNB-CU CP can also be configured into the gNB-DU by gNB-CU CP itself.

RAN2 agreed in RAN2#126 a CR R2-2405861 correcting Local Cartesian Coordinates in LPP. 
One change that can affect RAN3 is that RAN2 have specified a new element in the Relative Cartesian coordinates for local origin representation that indicates the horizontal axes orientation information for the reference point:

Extract from R2-2405861 starts here:
=======================================
NOTE 5:	The locations may be provided in either geodetic coordinates (RelativeLocation) or local Cartesian coordinates (RelativeCartesianLocation), but not both. 
======================================= End of extract.

Currently, in F1AP, the Relative Cartesian coordinates are defined in section 9.3.1.184 as the TRP Position Relative Cartesian IE, that refers to Relative Cartesian Location IE on 9.3.1.187 and is associated to a Reference Point IE defined in 9.3.1.188.

To align with LPP and CT4 specification, it is suggested to introduce the horizontal axes orientation information and Reference Point High Accuracy Access Position to the Reference Point IE, when the ReferencePoint in the  Reference Point IE CHOICE is set to Coordinate ID .  

However, due to NBC issue, it is not possible to add the IEs directly in 9.3.1.188 in the SEQUENCE (it is not extensible in ASN.1). Instead a BC solution that does not impact legacy functionality is to introduce an additional LocalOrigin IE as new CHOICE in the Reference point IE (9.3.1.188) that includes the Coordinate ID, Reference Point High Accuracy Access Position and horizontal axes orientation information.

The horizontal axes orientation information is added as mandatory information in the Local Origin IE to avoid IOT issues (i.e., sending the coordinate ID in different ways).

In RAN2#127 meeting, the following agreement was reached w.r.t L2 reset for intra-DU LTM. 
Since the gNB-DU is the entity performing the RLC reestablishment, the gNB-DU should be aware whether there is need to perform the RLC reestablishment during an intra-DU LTM. To achieve this purpose, two options can be considered:
Opt1: configure the ServingCellNoResetID and the noResetID of each candidate cell to the gNB-DU
Opt2: after gNB-CU receives the DU-CU Cell Switch Notification message, the gNB-CU triggers UE Context Modification procedure to indicate whether RLC reestablishment is needed or not.  

Compared with Opt1, Opt2 may delay the RLC re-establishment handling since it relies on the configuration from gNB-CU after triggering LTM. Moreover, the Opt1 is more aligned with RAN2’s design, and RAN3 determines to use the similar design for the UE based TA measurement. Thus, Opt1 is a preferable solution.

For RAN sharing with multiple cell ID broadcast, RAN3 has agreed that the entity controlling the involved gNB-DUs sharing the same physical cell resources decides whether “F1-U resources are established towards either all involved gNB-CUs or only some of them”(see 38.401 §7.7.2.3). If a gNB serves some cell resources for which RAN sharing by means of RAN sharing with multiple cell ID broadcast is not applied, and other cell resources for which this RAN sharing variant is applied, it might be beneficial to inform the gNB-DUs serving cell resources for which RAN sharing with multiple cell ID broadcast is applied about this fact.
This information may be taken into account by the entity controlling the involved gNB-DUs sharing the same physical cell resources when setting up F1-U tunnel resources.

In Rel-18 WID “NR support for dedicated spectrum less than 5MHz for FR1” a new 3 MHz Configurable Bandwidth has been introduced with a maximum transmission bandwidth of 15-PRBs, which is captured in TS 38.104. Such Transmission Bandwidth needs to be exchanged over F1 interface.

In multiple cell broadcasting scenario, when the gNB-DU initiated F1-U setup by using BROADCAST TRANSPORT RESOURCE REQUEST message, it is beneficial that the gNB-DU can include MRB ID IE and BC Bearer Context F1-U TNL Info at DU IE in the message. Then the gNB-CU-CP sends BROADCAST BEARER MODIFICATION REQUEST message to the gNB-CU-UP, including MRB ID IE and BC Bearer Context F1-U TNL Info at DU IE. 
Currently the F1-U tunnel Not Established IE is introduced per MBS Session, in such case, in some scenarios, the gNB-CU and gNB-DU has to establish F1-U tunnels multiple times for some area sessions. In order to fulfil the agreement and avoid unnecessary cost, it is needed to introduce the F1-U tunnel Not Established IE also in per Area Session granularity.

Mobile TRP Location information is provided to the gNB-CU, then to LMF via multiple messages. The Assigned Criticality for Mobile TRP Location information IE is set to “ignore” in Positioning Measurement Result IE and E-CID Measurement Result IE, but it is set to “reject” in TRP Information IE. The Assigned Criticality should be consistent for same IE.

When a predicted CCO issue is being signalled or cancelled, some IEs need to always be present, while other IEs need to have matching information.
In the Predicted CCO Assistance Information IE, the Predicted CCO Issue IE and the Predicted Affected Cells and Beams IE are always needed, and their presence should be mandatory.
Furthermore, whenever a predicted CCO issue is cancelled, the indicated cells and beams need to match the cells and beams of a previously signalled predicted CCO assistance information.
Therefore, the following case of abnormal conditions in the gNB-CU Configuration Update procedure may occur:
the gNB-DU receives a GNB-CU CONFIGURATION UPDATE message which includes the Predicted CCO Assistance Information IE with the Predicted CCO issue IE set to “cancel” but the listed cells and beams do not match the list of cells and beams contained in a previously received Predicted CCO Assistance Information IE.

For each periodic CSI-RS resource, the candidate gNB-DU provides each CSI-RS associated with pre-configured QCL-info (via qcl-InfoPeriodicCSI-RS, which indicates a TCI state ID). However, for Semi-Persistent CSI-RS, this is not possible. The reason is that Semi-Persistent CSI-RSs are pre-configured but activated dynamically, based on needs determined from periodic SSB or CSI-RS measurements.

Therefore, when the source gNB-DU selects an Semi-Persistent CSI-RS for activation, it also needs to determine the appropriate TCI State and indicate it to the candidate gNB-DU(s), this ensures that the Semi-Persistent CSI-RS can be properly activated with the correct TCI State.

Following is miscellaneous issues detected in XnAP:
The Future Coverage Modification Notification IE contains both mandatory (cell-level) and optional (beam-level) information. However, in the procedure for the “cancel” operation, the handling of these IEs is not consistently described.
The procedural text for the “cancel” operation should consistently refer to TS 38.401.
In the sentence “If the Predicted CCO Assistance Information IE is contained in the GNB-CU CONFIGURATION UPDATE message and the NR CGI IE contained in the Predicted Affected Cells and Beams IE is not served by the gNB-DU, the gNB-DU may use it to adjust the coverage of its cell(s) and optionally beam(s) configuration”, the word “Future” for configuration is not mentioned.
There is currently a misalignment in the terminology related to Performance Delay Monitoring between NR user plane and F1AP specifications.

With respect to the CU-DU Mobility Initiation Request message, the tabular and ASN.1 need to be aligned. 
In the message, the list of “SSB Index with measurement quantities” is transferred to the DU included in the Assistance Information IE and this is reflected in the tabular. However, in the ASN.1, single SSB Index and single CSI-RS with measurement quantities item is used instead of the list, which is clear misalignment with the tabular.
In the Candidate Cell with Beam Information List IE, the SSB Index List is optional in the tabular. It is not aligned to the ASN.1 where the list is defined as a mandatory field.

Two RACH configuration options are specified for SBFD RA in TS 38.331. A cell can configure only one RACH configuration option. This can be either: 1) A single RACH configuration that supports both non-SBFD RA operation and SBFD RA operation, or 2) A dual RACH configuration where a RACH configuration is used for non-SBFD RA operation and an additional RACH configuration is designated for SBFD RA operation. 
For option 2, the exchange of SBFD RACH configuration between NG-RAN is needed for RACH optimization. For CU/DU split case, gNB-DU provides SBFD RACH configuration to gNB-CU firstly and then gNB-CU further provide it to neighbour gNB-DU(s) by neighbour gNB-CU(s).

Current E-CID framework is designed on the concept of “one cell level measurement”, however one cell can comprise several measuring TRPs, which can report different measurements, e.g., AoA based on legacy SRS for MIMO signals.
To allow for multiple reporting of measurements, it is proposed to allow the gNB-DU to report Angle of Arrival per TRP measurements in the E-CID Measurement procedures by introducing a new dedicated measurement request type. This will improve the accuracy of E-CID positioning method.

records.scope: The present document provides the description and investigation of new AI/ML based use cases, i.e., Network Slicing and Coverage and Capacity Optimization, and its corresponding solutions, and initial analysis of Rel-18 leftovers.

records.conclusions: In this TR, failure scenario in the existing gNB-CU-CP architecture from various perspectives were studied. A failure affecting the entire (logical) gNB-CU-CP would impact all UEs served by the cells of the gNB-DUs connected to the gNB-CU-CP, resulting in those UEs being out of service for potentially long periods of time (dependent on type of failure and available resiliency measures). Current specification allows for some resiliency mechanisms via appropriate implementation (as described in TS 38.401[2]) which can address a number of the failure scenarios.
